---
title: "Atlas spaces and transforms"
---

A coordinate names a place in the brain only together with its space: the atlas, the origin,
the units and the scaling it was recorded in. This page explains the spaces of the IBL atlas
and how they relate. To cite an atlas or a scaling, see [Citations](../citations.qmd).

## The Allen CCF frame and the IBL frame

The Allen Common Coordinate Framework (CCF) is a volume, and the IBL frame is a way of writing
positions in that same volume. Every coordinate in the IBL atlas is in the IBL frame. The two
frames differ in where the origin is, what the units are, and which way each axis counts.

![The Allen CCF frame beside the IBL frame, on the same sagittal template slice. In the CCF the
origin is the corner of the volume; in the IBL frame it is bregma.](images/frames-allen-vs-ibl.svg){fig-alt="The same side view of the mouse brain twice, anterior on the left, inside the box that is the atlas volume. In the Allen CCF the origin is the anterior, dorsal, left corner, in micrometres, with AP increasing towards posterior and DV towards ventral. In the IBL frame the origin is bregma, in metres, with AP increasing towards anterior and DV towards dorsal."}

Bregma sits at ML 5739, AP 5400, DV 332 µm in the CCF volume. The signs and units of the IBL
frame are on [Coordinates and volumes](coordinates-and-volumes.qmd).

## The four atlases

Which atlas fits depends on where your coordinates come from.

| Your coordinates | Atlas |
|---|---|
| Histology, or a tool that registers data to the Allen CCF | **Allen** |
| A planned probe insertion, or stereotaxic coordinates on a live mouse | **Needles** or **MRI Toronto** |
| A plan made in Pinpoint's Qiu 2018 space | **Qiu 2018** |

## Coordinates from histology: the Allen atlas

The Allen atlas is the Allen CCF, an average of 1,675 mouse brains imaged by serial two-photon
tomography. Histology and registration tools place data in the CCF, so their coordinates are in
the Allen atlas. Its region annotations are the Allen 2017 release.

## Planning an insertion: the Needles, MRI Toronto and Qiu 2018 atlases

Stereotaxic coordinates are measured from bregma with the brain inside the skull. The Needles
and MRI Toronto atlases stretch the Allen CCF along each axis to fit an MRI atlas of the brain
in the skull, so their coordinates are closer to those used in surgery. The Qiu 2018 atlas has the
MRI Toronto scaling and adds a pitch.

| Atlas | Source | Acquisition | Subjects | ML | AP | DV | Pitch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Needles** | Dorr 2008 (DSURQE) | Post-mortem, brain in skull | 40 C57BL/6J, p84 | 1 | 1.087 | 0.952 | none |
| **MRI Toronto** | Qiu 2018 | In vivo | 12, p65 | 0.952 | 1.031 | 0.885 | none |
| **Qiu 2018** | Qiu 2018, as in Pinpoint | In vivo | 12, p65 | 0.952 | 1.031 | 0.885 | 5° |

The regions and their labels are the same in all four atlases; the scaling and the pitch change
only where a coordinate falls in the brain.

![Brain outlines of the Allen, Needles and MRI Toronto atlases on a coronal slice at AP −2 mm and
the midline sagittal slice, in metres from bregma. The slices are taken at the same coordinate in
each atlas, so they cut slightly different anatomy; the depth difference is largest.](images/scaling-overlay.png){fig-alt="Two panels of brain outlines in black, blue and red for the Allen, Needles and MRI Toronto atlases. The outlines share the dorsal surface at bregma and move apart towards the ventral side, with the MRI Toronto outline the shallowest."}

### The Qiu 2018 atlas and its 5° pitch

`Qiu2018Atlas` is `MRITorontoAtlas` followed by a rotation of 5° about the ML axis, with bregma as
the pivot. It follows the Qiu 2018 transform of [Pinpoint](https://virtualbrainlab.org/pinpoint/in_vivo_alignment.html),
which rotates the CCF to level the bregma-lambda surface, pitching it up by 5° (Birman et al.
2023, citing the International Brain Laboratory). Pinpoint's Dorr 2008 transform has the same
rotation on the Needles scaling, and its legacy IBL Dorr transform is the Needles scaling alone.
`NeedlesAtlas` is that legacy transform; `iblatlas` has no pitched Needles atlas.

- The scaling is applied first, then the rotation. Bregma is the pivot, so it stays at `(0, 0, 0)`.
- A positive `pitch`, in degrees, lifts the anterior side of the atlas: `Qiu2018Atlas(pitch=5.0)`
  is the default. The direction follows Pinpoint's description of the rotation, and has not been
  checked against a lambda coordinate.
- The rotation is in the atlas coordinates, not in the volumes. The image and annotation volumes
  are those of the Allen CCF, so data on the CCF grid stays aligned with the atlas.
- Converting points works: `xyz2ccf`, `ccf2xyz` and `get_labels` go through the rotation.
  Anything that needs the brain surface or the voxel size of an axis raises a `ValueError`,
  because the volume axes no longer line up with the atlas axes: the slice and surface plots
  (`plot_sslice`, `plot_top`, `compute_surface`), `get_labels(radius_um=...)` and the `Insertion`
  methods that use the surface (`Insertion.from_dict`, `get_brain_entry`). To draw a pitched
  slice, map the region contours through `atlas.bc.i2xyz`, as the figure below does. See
  [Coordinates and volumes](coordinates-and-volumes.qmd#atlases-with-a-rotation).

![The midline sagittal slice of the Allen, Needles, MRI Toronto and Qiu 2018 atlases, with
the regions drawn as polygons and all panels on the same limits. P1 to P3 are the same three
CCF voxels in every atlas and the cross is bregma. The Qiu 2018 atlas is the MRI Toronto atlas
rotated about bregma, so its posterior end sits lower.](images/atlas-variants-sagittal.png){fig-alt="Four sagittal slices of the mouse brain, anterior on the left, coloured by region: Allen, Needles, MRI Toronto and Qiu 2018. Three marked points sit in the olfactory bulb, the septum and the cerebellum in every panel. The brains get slightly shorter in depth from Allen to MRI Toronto, and the Qiu 2018 brain is tilted with its posterior end lower."}

The three marked voxels, to check a conversion. Each row is one CCF voxel and its position in
each atlas, in (ML, AP, DV) µm, relative to bregma for the atlases and from the corner of the
volume for the CCF.

| Point | Region | CCF | Allen | Needles | MRI Toronto | Qiu 2018 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | onl | 5739, 1400, 4332 | 0, 4000, -4000 | 0, 4348, -3808 | 0, 4124, -3540 | 0, 4417, -3167 |
| P2 | SF | 5739, 5400, 3332 | 0, 0, -3000 | 0, 0, -2856 | 0, 0, -2655 | 0, 231, -2645 |
| P3 | CENT3 | 5739, 11400, 3332 | 0, -6000, -3000 | 0, -6522, -2856 | 0, -6186, -2655 | 0, -5931, -3184 |

[Pinpoint](https://virtualbrainlab.org/pinpoint/in_vivo_alignment.html) is the tool many IBL
users plan in vivo trajectories with. It offers CCF, Qiu 2018, Dorr 2008 and a legacy IBL Dorr
transform. Its Qiu 2018 transform is `Qiu2018Atlas` and its legacy IBL Dorr transform is
`NeedlesAtlas`. Check that an `Insertion` and a Pinpoint plan are expressed in the same frame
before comparing them. State which tool produced a coordinate when you record it.
